elements.element: The licence extends to Customer's affiliates without a notice or consent condition.
elements.evidence: The grant expressly covers “affiliated companies of Sparkling” without requiring notice or consent.

elements.element: The licence extends to contractors acting on Customer's behalf.
elements.evidence: The grant expressly covers “contractors acting on Sparkling's behalf,” subject to the same Authorized Location restriction.
The rendered clause contains no perpetual-duration language. It does not demonstrate that paid-up licences are absent, so the conditional requirement cannot be treated as inapplicable.
The rendered clause contains no irrevocability protection. It does not demonstrate that paid-up licences are absent.

elements.element: A subscription licence may be terminated only for breach, and not for convenience or another reason.
elements.evidence: No restriction on termination of subscription licences appears in the rendered language, and subscription licences are not demonstrably absent.

elements.element: Any breach permitting termination of a subscription licence must be material.
elements.evidence: The rendered language does not establish material breach as the required termination threshold.

elements.element: A subscription licence may be terminated for material breach only if that breach remains uncured.
elements.evidence: The rendered language contains no cure requirement or uncured-breach trigger.

elements.element: The licence is transferable to any successor of Customer.
elements.evidence: Transferability is limited to a successor to Sparkling's business through merger, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all assets; it does not extend to successors generally.

elements.element: Customer's affiliates are covered upon Customer's written notice, without requiring consent.
elements.evidence: Affiliates are included automatically in the grant without notice or consent, which is broader than coverage upon written notice.

elements.element: The licence is transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction.
elements.evidence: The grant permits transfer to a successor to Sparkling's business by merger, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all assets, and Sections 3(c) and 20(d) remove the consent barrier for that transfer.

result.reason: The redline reaches the fallback and adds the preferred contractor coverage, but omits all required paid-up and subscription protections and limits successor transferability to specified M&A events. It is not minimal because contractor coverage is unnecessary to reach the fallback and, more significantly, Section 20(d) also grants Garman a new successor-assignment right. That reciprocal change alters an unrelated commercial restriction applicable to Garman, so the redline does not fully preserve the original intent.
